newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backeds firm, market girds for payrolls.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backeds firm, market girds for payrolls.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities prices were higher late this session and participants reported heightened down-in-coupon activity as well as some movement from mortgage-backeds into Treasuries.

Market players agreed all eyes would be on the June payrolls report due Friday, but some direction to prices may be provided on Thursday by the July Chicagoland Business Barometer and the June help wanted index.
One veteran market observer said the rally in Treasury prices, which has sent the 10-year note yield down to 6.05 percent, has prompted prepayment concerns.

Participants said 7.5 percent mortgage coupons would become refinanceable if the 10-year Treasury note declines 20 basis points below 6.05 percent, "We have had a quick move from 6.25 percent to 6.05 percent, which has investors very nervous," said one market observer.
Early Wednesday, investors shifted from mortgage-backeds into Treasuries. The movement into lower coupons was expected to step up if 10-year Treasuries decline below 6 percent.
Hedging in response to lower interest rates is common, but one New York mortgage-backed products salesman said some mortgage originators had been "laissez faire" about it.

Late in the session, Government National Mortgage Association 7.5 percent coupons were up 10/32 at 101 31/32 to offer a bond equivalent yield of 7.21. Federal National Mortgage Association 7.5 percent coupons were up 8/32 at 101 25/32 and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp 7.5 percent coupons were up 7/32 at 101 31/32.
Meanwhile, the Treasury's 10-year note was up 14/32 at 104 7/32 to yield 6.05.
"People are stepping up their hedging going into tomorrow's and Friday's numbers," said the New York salesman, noting that much of the down-in-coupon movement is out of 8.0-percent coupon MBS.

The New York salesman said mortgage loan servicers have been busy hedging their mortgage servicing portfolios with interest rate floors. Also, some mortgage bankers were buying a put or selling a call on an MBS, the salesman said.
"They do some of each because they want a balance to limit their exposure," he said, noting that the heightened hedging activity just ahead of an employment report is not unussual.
In the MBS derivatives sector, spreads on interest-only securities (IOs) were wider, according to a New York IO trader.

Lists of IOs and inverse floaters were out for the bid this session, he said. "IOs got really beat up. We saw a couple up lists which traded wider," he said noting that in recent sessionss IO spreads widened for the first time in two to three months.
While IOs were expected see their prices decline in a lower rate environment, the current market has a different investor base and is "more technical so it (price declines) should be more orderly."
IOs are sold at a deep discount to their notional principal amount. They have no par value or face value; IOs increase in value when interest rates rise and prepayments slow.
"Some benchmark trusts are falling twice as much as we would have anticipated," the trader said, noting that IOs may tighten in spreads to Treasuries in coming weeks.
